decks.name: Anatomy III: Cranial Nerves, Brainstem & Spinal Cord (Board Review)

cards.vorderseite: Cranial nerves with parasympathetic fibers and their ganglia
cards.rueckseite:
- **CN III** (Edinger–Westphal) → **ciliary** ganglion → sphincter pupillae, ciliary muscle
- **CN VII** (superior salivatory) → greater petrosal → **pterygopalatine** ganglion (lacrimal, nasal glands); chorda tympani → **submandibular** ganglion (submandibular, sublingual)
- **CN IX** (inferior salivatory) → Jacobson nerve → lesser petrosal → **otic** ganglion → parotid
- **CN X** (dorsal motor nucleus) → intramural ganglia (thorax/abdomen)

cards.vorderseite: Oculomotor nerve: course and pupillary fibers
cards.rueckseite:
Nucleus at the **superior colliculus** level; fascicles pass the red nucleus, exit medial to the cerebral peduncle, run **between PCA and SCA**, lateral to PComm, into the **roof/lateral wall of the cavernous sinus**, through the **superior orbital fissure within the anulus of Zinn**.
Superior division: superior rectus, levator. Inferior division: medial/inferior rectus, inferior oblique + parasympathetics.
Pupillomotor fibers are **superficial/dorsomedial** → compressive lesions (aneurysm, uncal herniation) affect the pupil early; ischemic (diabetic) palsy spares it.

- **Superior rectus** subnucleus projects to the **contralateral** superior rectus
- **Levator** (central caudal subnucleus): single midline nucleus → **bilateral** ptosis with nuclear lesions
- Other muscles ipsilateral

Only cranial nerve that:
1. exits from the **dorsal** brainstem (below the inferior colliculus)
2. **fully decussates** (in the superior medullary velum)
3. decussates **outside** the nucleus (outside the CNS proper)
4. is the thinnest, with the longest intracranial course
Innervates the **contralateral superior oblique** (intorsion, depression in adduction). Palsy → vertical diplopia, head tilt **away** from the lesion.

- **Mesencephalic:** proprioception (jaw); contains **first-order neurons** in the CNS; jaw jerk afferent
- **Principal (chief) sensory** (pons): fine touch
- **Spinal nucleus** (pons → C2): **pain and temperature**; onion-skin (perioral rostral, lateral face caudal)
- **Motor nucleus:** muscles of mastication, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, anterior digastric

zeilen: CN III, IV, V1 (lacrimal, frontal, nasociliary), VI, superior ophthalmic vein
V3, accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve
Middle meningeal artery/vein, meningeal branch of V3
Nothing passes through (ICA over it; vidian nerve/artery at its edge)
CN VII, nervus intermedius, VIII, labyrinthine artery
Pars nervosa: CN IX (+ inferior petrosal sinus); pars vascularis: CN X, XI, IJV

cards.vorderseite: Abducens nerve: course and why it is so vulnerable
cards.rueckseite:
Nucleus in the **pontine tegmentum** (under the facial colliculus); exits at the **pontomedullary junction**, ascends the clivus, passes under the **petroclinoid (Gruber) ligament in Dorello canal**, runs **free in the cavernous sinus lateral to the ICA**, enters the orbit through the anulus of Zinn.
Long course → **false localizing sign** of raised ICP; also petrous apicitis (**Gradenigo**: VI palsy, retro-orbital pain, otorrhea).

cards.vorderseite: Abducens nucleus vs. nerve lesion; internuclear ophthalmoplegia
cards.rueckseite:
**Nerve:** ipsilateral lateral rectus palsy.
**Nucleus** (contains interneurons to the contralateral MLF): **ipsilateral horizontal gaze palsy** of both eyes (often with facial palsy).
**MLF lesion (INO):** ipsilateral **adduction failure** + abducting nystagmus of the other eye, convergence preserved. Bilateral INO: MS (young), stroke (elderly).
**One-and-a-half syndrome:** PPRF/abducens nucleus + MLF.

Motor fibers loop around the **abducens nucleus (facial colliculus)**, exit at the pontomedullary junction with nervus intermedius → IAC (**anterosuperior** quadrant) → labyrinthine segment (narrowest) → **geniculate ganglion** (greater petrosal nerve) → tympanic segment → mastoid segment (**nerve to stapedius**, then **chorda tympani**) → **stylomastoid foramen** → parotid: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical.
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 71–73. IAC mnemonic "Seven-up, Coke down".

cards.vorderseite: Facial palsy: upper vs. lower motor neuron
cards.rueckseite:
**UMN (central):** forehead spared (bilateral cortical input to the upper face) → contralateral lower face weakness; emotional smiling may be preserved.
**LMN (peripheral, e.g. Bell palsy):** entire ipsilateral face; depending on level also **hyperacusis** (stapedius), loss of **taste** anterior ⅔ (chorda), reduced **lacrimation** (greater petrosal: lesion at/proximal to geniculate).

Spiral ganglion → **cochlear nuclei** → (trapezoid body, **superior olive**) → **lateral lemniscus** → **inferior colliculus** → **MGB** → **Heschl gyrus** (41/42).
Bilateral representation above the cochlear nuclei → a unilateral central lesion does **not** cause unilateral deafness; unilateral deafness = cochlea, nerve or cochlear nucleus.
Acoustic reflex: superior olive → VII (stapedius) and V (tensor tympani).

Four nuclei (superior, inferior, medial, lateral).
**Lateral (Deiters) nucleus** → ipsilateral **lateral vestibulospinal tract** → extensor (antigravity) tone (decerebrate rigidity when released).
Medial nucleus → **medial vestibulospinal tract**/MLF → neck muscles, eye–head coordination (vestibulo-ocular reflex).
Utricle → superior vestibular nerve; saccule → inferior vestibular nerve.

- **Sensory:** posterior ⅓ of tongue (taste + general), pharynx, middle ear (**Jacobson nerve**), **carotid sinus and body** (baroreflex/chemoreflex via nucleus solitarius) → afferent limb of **gag reflex**
- **Motor:** stylopharyngeus only (nucleus ambiguus)
- **Parasympathetic:** parotid via lesser petrosal → otic ganglion
Glossopharyngeal neuralgia: throat/ear pain triggered by swallowing, may cause syncope.

cards.vorderseite: Vagus nerve: nuclei and recurrent laryngeal course
cards.rueckseite:
**Nucleus ambiguus:** pharynx, larynx, palate (efferent limb of gag reflex). **Dorsal motor nucleus:** parasympathetic viscera. **Nucleus solitarius:** visceral afferents, taste (epiglottis).
**Recurrent laryngeal:** loops under the **subclavian artery on the right** and the **aortic arch on the left** (longer, more vulnerable) → all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid (superior laryngeal nerve). Right RLN at greater risk in anterior cervical approaches by some accounts (shorter, more oblique).

**CN XI (spinal):** from C1–C5 anterior horn cells, ascends through the foramen magnum, exits through the **jugular foramen** → SCM and trapezius. Lesion: shoulder droop, weak head turning **away** from the lesion.
**CN XII:** exits between pyramid and olive, through the **hypoglossal canal**; tongue deviates **toward** the side of an LMN lesion (unopposed contralateral genioglossus).

zeilen: Ipsilateral face pain/temp loss, Horner, ataxia, dysphagia/hoarseness (ambiguus), vertigo; contralateral body pain/temp loss; motor spared
Ipsilateral tongue weakness (XII); contralateral hemiparesis and loss of proprioception
Ipsilateral VI and VII palsy + contralateral hemiplegia
Ipsilateral gaze palsy, VII palsy + contralateral hemiplegia
Quadriplegia, anarthria; vertical eye movements/blinking preserved

cards.rueckseite:
**Locus coeruleus:** pigmented nucleus in the rostral pons/floor of 4th ventricle; main **norepinephrine** source, widespread projections, cortical activation and REM sleep.
**Raphe nuclei:** midline brainstem; main **serotonin** source (sleep, pain modulation via descending projections).

cards.vorderseite: Spinal cord and conus level by age
cards.rueckseite:
3rd fetal month: cord fills the canal. **Birth: conus ~L3**. **Adult: L1–L2**. A conus below L2 in adults suggests **tethered cord**.
C1 has no dorsal root (no dermatome). Cervical roots exit **above** their pedicle (C8 between C7 and T1), thoracic/lumbar roots **below** theirs.

zeilen: Clarke nucleus (C8–L2/L3), intermediolateral column (T1–L2, sympathetic; S2–S4 parasympathetic)
Dorsal columns (gracile medial = legs, cuneate lateral = arms)
Within 1–2 segments (anterior white commissure); sacral fibers lateral
Pyramidal decussation; legs lateral, arms medial

cards.vorderseite: Syringomyelia / central cord: why the sensory loss is dissociated
cards.rueckseite: A central lesion first interrupts **crossing spinothalamic fibers** in the anterior white commissure → **bilateral cape-like loss of pain and temperature** at the involved segments, with **preserved touch/proprioception** (dorsal columns). Expansion → anterior horn (LMN arm atrophy) and later long tracts.

- **Transverse atlantal ligament:** holds the dens against C1 (main stabilizer; part of the cruciate ligament)
- **Alar ligaments:** dens → occipital condyles/foramen magnum margins; limit rotation
- **Apical ligament:** dens tip → basion
- **Tectorial membrane:** rostral continuation of the PLL to the clivus
- ALL continues as the anterior atlanto-occipital membrane

cards.vorderseite: Superior orbital fissure vs. anulus of Zinn
cards.rueckseite:
**Inside** the anulus (oculomotor foramen): **CN III (superior + inferior division), nasociliary (V1), CN VI**.
**Outside / above** the anulus: **CN IV, frontal and lacrimal nerves (V1)**, superior ophthalmic vein.
Optic nerve and ophthalmic artery pass through the optic canal within the ring.
Mnemonic: "Lazy French Tarts Lie Naked In Anticipation" (lateral → medial).

**Optic strut:** bony bar between optic canal and superior orbital fissure (removed in anterior clinoidectomy).
**Falciform ligament:** dural fold over the optic nerve at the canal entrance between anterior clinoid and planum; opening it decompresses the nerve.

1st neuron: **hypothalamus** → brainstem → **ciliospinal center (C8–T2)**.
2nd neuron (preganglionic): T1 → over the **lung apex** → **superior cervical ganglion**.
3rd neuron: along the **ICA** → cavernous sinus → with V1 (long ciliary nerves) → dilator pupillae, Müller muscle; sweat fibers follow the ECA.
Signs: ptosis, miosis, (anhidrosis). Causes: Wallenberg, Pancoast tumor, carotid dissection, cluster headache.
